title: QuasiCoherentSymmetricAlgebraCore
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $F$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $S=P^\#$ and $j$ be the explicitly constructed symmetric algebra sheaf and degree-one map [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. For every commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra sheaf $B$ [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf] and linear map $f:F\to B$, there is a unique morphism $t:S\to B$ with $t_U(j_U(x))=f_U(x)$ for all opens $U$ and sections $x$.

source.place: Modules, Section 01CF (section-symmetric-exterior, line 3262: definition of Sym(F) as a quotient of the tensor algebra), Lemma 01CG (lemma-local-tensor-algebra, line 3303: Sym^n F is the sheafification of U -> Sym^n_{O(U)}(F(U))), Lemma 01CL (lemma-whole-tensor-algebra-permanence, line 3461: Sym of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent); Schemes, Section 01LA item (9) (schemes.tex line 4717); used as Sym^*_{O_X} in Properties, Lemmas 05JS, 086N, 0817

proof.text: *Step 3 (the universal property (a)).* Let $(\mathcal B,\tau)$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras and $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal B$ $\mathcal O_X$-linear. Existence: for each open $U$, $\mathcal B(U)$ is a commutative $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra via $\tau_U$ and $u_U$ is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear, so there is a unique $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map $b_U:\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$ with $b_U\iota_U=u_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. For $V\subseteq U$, $b_V\rho_{UV}$ and $(\cdot)|_V\circ b_U$ are $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra maps $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(V)$ which agree on $\iota_U(s)$ (both give $u_V(s|_V)=u_U(s)|_V$), so they are equal; thus $b:\mathcal P\to\mathcal B$ is a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings with $b\circ(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P)=\tau$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](1) there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of rings $\tilde u:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)\to\mathcal B$ with $\tilde u\theta=b$; then $\tilde u\sigma=b\circ(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P)=\tau$, so $\tilde u$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, and $\tilde u j_{\mathcal F}=\tilde u\theta\iota=b\iota=u$. Uniqueness: if $\tilde u'$ is a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras with $\tilde u'j_{\mathcal F}=u$, then $(\tilde u'\theta)_U$ is an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$ with $(\tilde u'\theta)_U\iota_U=u_U$, hence equals $b_U$; so $\tilde u'\theta=b=\tilde u\theta$ and $\tilde u'=\tilde u$ by the uniqueness in the sheafification property.
